title: It cheats death. It does not skip ageing.
description:
It cheats death. It does not skip ageing. Turritopsis dohrnii can revert from an adult jellyfish back into its earlier polyp stage when it is stressed, injured, or ageing. That part is real and published.

Described the reversal in the Biological Bulletin, using the phrase escaping death and achieving potential immortality, a title that outran the caveats inside its own paper.

Their colonies still get old. Aquarists who maintain polyp stock for years report it turning fragile after about six years: fewer healthy jellies, weaker responses. Reversing a life stage is not the same as not ageing.

Even the biologist who wrote it up says: I'm not convinced.
